The final geometry of an ORCA transition-state optimisation and of a Gaussian single point, written into a
separate folder with `--out-dir`.

**Files used** (from the repository):

* `files/orb.out` — ORCA, B3LYP-D4/def2-TZVP OptTS Freq, 37 atoms
* `tests/data/gaussian_ref/gaussian/g04_ticl4.log` — Gaussian 16, B3LYP/def2-TZVP single point, TiCl₄

**1. One XYZ per input.**

```bash
frog-xyz files/orb.out tests/data/gaussian_ref/gaussian/g04_ticl4.log --out-dir xyz
```

```text
✔  Saved xyz: xyz/orb_final.xyz
✔  Saved xyz: xyz/g04_ticl4_final.xyz
```

`xyz/g04_ticl4_final.xyz`:

```text
5
FROG formatted
Ti     0.000000     0.000000     0.000000
Cl     1.252850     1.252850     1.252850
Cl     1.252850    -1.252850    -1.252850
Cl    -1.252850     1.252850    -1.252850
Cl    -1.252850    -1.252850     1.252850
```

`xyz/orb_final.xyz` (first 6 lines):

```text
37
FROG formatted
 C    -1.157477     0.901492    -2.243442
 C    -1.306709     0.715679    -3.666027
 C    -2.381869     1.393214    -1.473934
 C    -2.087467     2.102121    -0.177313
…
```

* The Gaussian geometry is taken from the input orientation: Ti at the origin and the four Cl at
  (±1.252850, ±1.252850, ±1.252850) Å, a regular tetrahedron.
* The comment line is always `FROG formatted`. Charge and multiplicity are not stored, so write
  them into the next input yourself. `orb.out` is an anion (charge −1).
* Without `--out-dir` the files go next to the inputs (`files/orb_final.xyz`). ORCA's own `orb.xyz` is
  not touched, because of the `_PAC` suffix.
